165,000 new jobs:
what it means for you

lines.say: Economists expected fifty-nine thousand jobs. October delivered one hundred sixty-five thousand.

lines.text: That's from this morning's jobs report, and unemployment dipped to 4.1%.
lines.say: That's from this morning's jobs report, and unemployment dipped to four point one percent.

lines.text: That's nearly three times the forecast, after a year of mostly slow hiring.
lines.say: That's nearly three times the forecast, after a year of mostly slow hiring.

lines.text: Even September got a do-over. It was first reported at 29,000, and now it's 60,000.

lines.text: Paychecks grew too. Average hourly pay is up 3.1% from a year ago.
lines.say: Paychecks grew too. Average hourly pay is up three point one percent from a year ago.

lines.text: But prices rose 3.7% in the year through September, so average pay is still losing that race.

post.title: US added 165,000 jobs in October, far above forecasts
post.ig:
Economists expected 59,000 jobs. October delivered 165,000.
The October jobs report (BLS, Nov 6, 2026): payrolls +165,000 vs. a 59,000 Dow Jones forecast; unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%.
September was revised up to 60,000 from 29,000.
Average hourly pay rose 3.1% over the year, but consumer prices rose 3.7% in the year through September.
Before the report, markets priced about a 70% chance of a Fed rate hike on Dec. 9.
Sources: BLS via CNBC, Bloomberg, Yahoo Finance (Nov 6, 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
